lines: In Japan, they say a small green creature waits in every quiet river.
It is called the kappa, with a turtle shell and a beak.
On its head sits a dish of water, and that water is its power.
Legend says it grabs anyone who wanders too close to the bank.
One evening, a traveler heard a splash behind him.
The kappa leapt out, reaching with its webbed hands.
But he remembered the old advice, and bowed politely.
The kappa bowed back, so deeply that its water spilled out.
Weak and tame, it slipped back into the river.
title: The Tiny River Monster That Bows Back #shorts
description:
In Japanese folklore the kappa waits in quiet rivers, and its power is a dish of water on its head. One old trick is said to defeat it: good manners.
